From top companies like Google and Apple to tiny startups vying for your attention, Verge Tech has the latest in what matters in technology daily. Framework gave its 12-inch laptop some hardware upgrades The Laptop 12 has new Intel chips, a Linux option, a fingerprint reader, and a backlit keyboard. Jess Weatherbed 7 seconds ago Robin Williams’ Instagram account brought back to fight ‘AI abuse’ Zelda, Zak, and Cody Williams say their father’s Instagram account will be a ‘trusted place’ to share photos, videos, and memories. Emma Roth Aug 18 Latest In Tech Dominic Preston Two hours ago New Googlebook announcements are coming in September. It’s been a few months since Google revealed its Chromebook successor / sibling , and all’s been quiet since — at least officially, with leaks of laptops from Lenovo and Asus . We’ll know more soon: Google invited outlets including The Verge to a media event in September where we’ll get to “test out the laptops and new features.” Google makes it official: Googlebook launch event set for September in NYC [ Chrome Unboxed - The Latest Chrome OS News ] Richard Lawler Aug 18 Bugatti’s Tourbillon-inspired MicroLED TV twists, turns, and unfolds. While checking out the 1,800-horsepower Destrier that Bugatti unveiled at Monterey Car Week, the folks at Road & Track also got a taste of the carmaker’s C-Seed Bugatti N1 TV . Inspired by another 1,800hp beast , its sculptural design unfurls the 110- or 137-inch TV hiding inside in 45 seconds and can rotate up to 180 degrees. Jay Peters Aug 18 Meta’s smart glasses are now prohibited for ICE staffers. The glasses “could unintentionally capture, record or transmit sensitive information, potentially compromising privacy and legal protections,” ICE acting director David Venturella said in a memo to staff, according to The New York Times . Staffers can’t wear the glasses in the “federal workspace.” ICE Bars Its Workers From Wearing Meta’s Smart Glasses on the Job [ The New York Times ] Richard Lawler Aug 18 Claude can do more with Gmail and Google Drive, and access to Claude Cowork is expanding. A pair of announcements from Anthropic today include the word that access to Claude Cowork on mobile and web interfaces has rolled out to all paid accounts, so you can keep an eye on what it’s doing for you in more places . Separately, the Google Workspace connectors for Claude now support sending emails in Gmail and managing files in Google Drive — more details here . Image: Anthropic Andrew Liszewski Aug 18 Ikea is teasing a collaboration with Xbox. The Swedish flatpack furniture maker shared a video through its Instagram account today that seemingly reveals an upcoming collection inspired by the console. The video’s details are vague but it appears to show a piece of furniture inspired by an Xbox controller’s thumbstick as well as a bright green X-shaped cushion. Screenshot: Instagram Emma Roth Aug 18 Epic calls Apple’s new EU rates “junk fees.” The company responded to Apple’s new App Store policies in a post on X , claiming the updated fees “do nothing to open up the mobile app ecosystem to competition” and “deliberately violate” the EU’s Digital Markets Act. Screenshot: @EpicNewsroom via X Dominic Preston Aug 18 Android’s “advanced” sideloading flow is now live. Google’s Mishaal Rahman took to r/Android to announce the process, which will eventually be the only way to install apps from unverified Android developers. Verification enforcement kicks in globally in 2027, though in some countries begins next month. Enabling the one-time advanced flow now gets the mandatory 24-hour cooldown out of the way. We’re rolling out the advanced flow for installing apps from unverified developers [ Reddit ] OpenAI lays out new security changes after its AI hacked Hugging Face Jay Peters Aug 18 Jess Weatherbed Aug 18 Gemini in Chrome has landed on Android. After starting to roll out to “select devices” in June, Google’s AI Chrome assistant is now available to all Android users in the US. It adds a Gemini icon to the top-right of your toolbar that opens the familiar chatbot window, allowing Gemini to summarize web pages, answer questions, generate images, and more. You can see the Gemini sparkle icon now sitting beside your tab menu on the Chrome toolbar. Image: Google Lauren Feiner Aug 18 Meta says states can’t prove it lied about safety risks. The company laid out its defense in the trial against a coalition of state AGs, previewing that it will call on their own public health officials to combat claims of social media addiction, and claiming that the states have pulled public statements out of context to claim it misled parents. Jay Peters Aug 18 Spotify’s new Running Mode is now available on Android. The feature, which initially launched on iOS , offers preset playlists for running. It’s available to Premium subscribers in the US, Canada, the UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, and Sweden on both mobile platforms, Spotify says. How to Get the Most Out of Running Mode [ Spotify ] PlayStation’s wireless gaming speakers launch in November Jay Peters Aug 18 Lauren Feiner Aug 18 Meta has constructed ‘tissue paper barriers’ to teens’ overuse of its platforms, AGs allege. In an opening statement, California deputy AG Megan O’Neill accused Meta of doing “too little, too late” to curb teens’ problematic usage of Facebook and Instagram, while misleading the public. She also laid out the states allegations that Meta knew — but didn’t remove – many kids under 13 on its platforms. Apple squashes EU beef with new App Store rules Emma Roth and Jay Peters Aug 18 Tesla is finally launching the Cybercab — let’s hope it’s ready Andrew J. Hawkins Aug 18 Jay Peters Aug 18 Konami’s Apple Arcade Castlevania game is shutting down. Castlevania: Grimoire of Souls , which featured classic characters from the series and launched in 2021, will become unavailable to download on August 20th and will be fully shut down on September 3rd, Konami says . Symphony of the Night composer Michiru Yamane worked on the game, and we interviewed her back when it came out. Important Notice Regarding the End of Service [ Castlevania -Grimoire of Souls- Official Website ] Nilay Patel Aug 18 Honestly I’d take the PowerBook Duo. The pricing spread on items in the new early Apple / Steve Jobs auction is wild. A pair of signed Steve Jobs business cards is going for six figures, and the disparity in Apple devices is distinctly tilted towards the modern era, as seen here. Jess Weatherbed Aug 18 GeForce Now comes to Firefox. Nvidia’s cloud gaming service can now stream more than 5,000 PC games directly in the Mozilla browser, joining existing support for Chrome, Safari, Edge, and Opera GX. It’s the latest effort to get GeForce Now onto as many screens as possible, following its expansions to Linux and Amazon Fire TV this year. Firefox Nvidia GeForce Now partnership | The Mozilla Blog [ Mozilla ] Andrew Liszewski Aug 18 They hear me rollin’. Segway’s new $449.99 S2 Kids self-balancing scooter is a direct descendent of the brand’s original Personal Transporter but includes upgrades like animated RGB lighting and built-in Bluetooth speakers for blasting music. It’s got a top speed of 8.7 mph, a range of eight miles, and a weight limit of up to 132 pounds. If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. 1 / 4 Image: Segway Jess Weatherbed Aug 18 Nothing is about to drop its own budget ‘Neo.’ Buds Neo, that is, which are being teased by Nothing’s budget-friendly CMF sub-brand, just two weeks after it launched the CMF Clip Pro open earbuds . It posted the below image on X yesterday as a “hint of what’s next.” A new video posted today also shows colorful Smart Dial charging case configurations, and a short message: “Buds Neo. 20 August.” These upcoming CMF wireless earbuds are similar in shape to the Buds 2 Plus that the brand launched last year. Image: Nothing Lauren Feiner Aug 18 Meta faces a kids safety trial that could cost it hundreds of billions of dollars. Beginning at 11 AM Eastern, you can stream opening arguments in a trial where 29 attorneys general allege Meta harmed consumers through addictive design. Meta denies this, and warned damages could reach $1.4 trillion — nearing its market cap. The AGs say they’d likely be closer to $200 billion . US District Court Northern District of California Livestream [ YouTube ] Andrew Liszewski Aug 18 The new Fairphone 6 Plus gets a perfect repairability score. Given it’s a minor hardware refresh of last year’s Fairphone 6 it comes as no surprise that the new Fairphone 6 Plus (the company’s first smartphone it will sell directly in the US) was awarded a perfect 10/10 score in iFixit’s teardown test. Disassembly of everything from camera modules to the screen was straightforward using just basic tools. Comcast is turning millions of its routers into motion detectors Jennifer Pattison Tuohy Aug 18 Firefox’s Smart Window promises a better AI browser Stevie Bonifield Aug 18 Polaroid’s new Pokémon collection captures memories, not Pikachus Andrew Liszewski Aug 18 Jess Weatherbed Aug 18 Spirit in the machine. Google won a $10 million bankruptcy auction to acquire a hefty collection of business data from the now defunct Spirit Airlines , which it plans to use for AI training. The data, which includes calendar info, documents, spreadsheets, emails, and employee chats will be “deidentified,” a Google spokesperson said in a statement to Axios : “We will not receive any personal information from this dataset. Any data we receive will be rigorously scrubbed of any personally identifiable information by a third party before receipt.” Google’s Pet Memory forgot who my cats are Gemini for Home promises its Nest cameras can recognize my cats by name — but it can’t tell Boone from Smokey, making pet-focused smart notifications and automations mostly useless. Jennifer Pattison Tuohy Aug 18 The Verge Guide to Pets Kara Verlaney Aug 18 My parrot ate my keyboard John Higgins Aug 18 Oops! My cat is an iPad kid He has his own games and favorite YouTube shows. Jess Weatherbed Aug 18 How I turned my fish tank high tech These gadgets made a huge difference in how I care for my fish. Emma Roth Aug 18 Elon Musk broke the FAA — Palantir is picking up the pieces Musk’s DOGE was supposed to rebuild the nation’s air traffic control system, but it ended up paving the way for Peter Thiel’s company to take over. Darryl Campbell Aug 18 Fairphone’s latest repairable phone is going on sale in the US Dominic Preston Aug 18 Jess Weatherbed Aug 18 Right-clicking without the clutter. Microsoft’s latest Experimental Windows 11 Insider Preview build introduces support for Emoji 17.0, alongside an updated context menu experience in File Explorer that’s “designed to feel faster, cleaner, and easier to tailor.” A notable personalization feature finally lets you add the “Print” command to the context menu in Windows 11. The “Customize menu” option at the bottom of the new context window takes you to a settings page where you can choose which file actions to enable. Image: Microsoft Jess Weatherbed Aug 18 Google is reportedly stopping Pixel production in China. Most of Google’s products are still manufactured in the country, but Nikkei Asia reports that all production of Pixel phones, watches and earbuds will leave China starting in 2027. Google started this exodus in 2019 , shifting to building production capacity in Vietnam and India instead, as have Apple and Microsoft in recent years. Google is reportedly planning to move all Pixel production out of China - Engadget [ Engadget ] Apple’s camera-equipped AirPods appear in leaked video Jess Weatherbed Aug 18 Dominic Preston Aug 18 Google’s people-tracking app is now on Wear OS. Find Hub on Google-powered smartwatches now includes a separate Find People app. As 9to5Google notes, it’s barebones: it shows a list of everyone you’re sharing location with, but to actually change any settings or see their location on a map, you have to open your phone. Perhaps there’s more to come. Find Hub for Wear OS adds very basic ‘Find people’ app [ 9to5Google ] Reddit’s AI is turning posts into podcasts and short videos Jay Peters Aug 17 Travis Larchuk Aug 17 Today’s Vergecast: The Digital Doctor will see you now. A few years ago, Leo Mastrolia started a gadget repair shop. Little did he know he’d eventually become known across the internet as The Digital Doctor , and would learn to fix practically every gadget you can think of. On this episode, which is part one of our conversation with Leo, he tells us about his journey as a gadget fixer, the growth of his social channels, and how right-to-repair fights and upgrade cycles are affecting life in his store. Watch | Listen | Get ad-free Richard Lawler Aug 17 Bloomberg: Andreesen Horowitz is the focus of an antitrust investigation. According to Bloomberg , a “nearly year-old investigation” is looking into the possibility that a16z “investment partners are improperly serving on the boards of competing artificial intelligence companies.” Co-founder Ben Horowitz is on the board of Databricks, while partner Martin Casado was on the board of dbt labs before it was acquired by Fivetran, where he now holds a seat.
